title: Roadmap — 8 Aug 2026 → 31 May 2027
subtitle: 42 weeks · 1146 h planned · every day named
audience: Every domain an interviewer could ask about tomorrow carries a non-zero allocation every single week. Depth rotates on top of a permanent baseline.

sprints.note: The sanitizer alias is week 1. It is the thing that lost the 7 Aug OA.
C++ depth. Everything else holds its baseline, so you stay interview-ready throughout.
A real Postgres on day 1. Python rises because it is the prerequisite for P1.
DBMS depth finishes; P1 gains weight. Networks gets its one block.
LLD depth — starting with LRU, the question that ended Teradata.
P1 ships this sprint: live URL, CI green. Last high-capacity sprint before 1 Feb.
Capacity drops to 23 h. HLD is the domain that rises at placement. 28 Feb is the 1900 decision.
Consolidate. Start nothing new. Defend or remove every resume bullet.

items.res: Resume-bullet audit: 3 questions each, answer in writing
items.note: Every technology on your resume in one column. Next to each: could you answer three questions on it right now? The estimate is ~6 solid, ~5 partial, ~9 absent — your job today is to verify or refute that.

items.label: D14
items.title: Set up the sanitizer alias — and prove it fires
items.note: Put `alias g++dbg='g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG -Wall -Wextra'` in your shell rc. Then write a 5-line program that reads v[v.size()] and confirm ASan reports it. Twenty minutes. This is the single item that lost the 7 Aug OA.

items.label: D14
items.title: Rebuild the 7 Aug failure under the alias
items.note: priority_queue<pair<int,vector<int>>> — reproduce the exact segfault, then run it under the alias. Write down which sanitizer caught it and how many seconds it took.

items.label: P1
items.title: P1 scope on one page
items.res: PROJECT P1 — properly-built backend service (20 rows)
items.note: The 20 resume rows this service has to make true, written down. Build nothing today. Getting the scope wrong costs 110 h.

items.label: D14
items.title: Comparator rule card: strict weak ordering
items.note: comp(a,a) must be false. Write a comparator that violates it, run it under -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG, and keep the crash output in your error log. This is the other half of what went wrong.

items.label: D05
items.title: Get a real Postgres running
items.res: My notes: DBMS practical + theory tracks
items.at: p24 · 4 The Relational Model: Tables and Keys
items.note: `docker run --name pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -p 5432:5432 -d postgres:16`, then psql in and \d your way around. Everything in D05 after today runs against this, not against notes.

items.label: D14
items.title: Build the stress harness
items.note: brute.cpp + fast.cpp + gen.cpp + a 20-line bash loop. Put it where you can paste it in 30 seconds under exam pressure.
